curl returned HTTP 301 with an empty body; the redirect was not followed.
Only the first 100000 characters were read through WebFetch (entries newer than about 2025-09). Raw curl grep covered the whole file for a few keywords only.
Not attempted; it is a blog post outside this lane. It surfaced in search and is where the SAP benchmark method would live.

cards.source_date: undated page, read 2026-11-04; changelog shows v0 release 0.226.3 on 2026-10-27
cards.quote: BAML v1 is a separate, fully featured programming language in public beta.
cards.claim: The public docs site now documents only BAML v0, called the legacy DSL. BAML v1 is a different language with docs this site does not link. v0 is still releasing (0.226.3, 2026-10-27, TLS and CA trust updates). Every page, the Studio page and the changelog carry the same notice. Boundary Studio v1 was also slated for deprecation by end of March 2026.
cards.evidence: Version notice at the top of every page fetched; changelog table shows 0.225.0 (2026-07-31) moving BEP analysis to v1 and branding older releases v0. The docs give no end-of-life statement for v0 and no v1 link.
cards.first_guess: No landing in the harness. It corrects the assumption that BAML is one stable tool: any later evaluation must name v0 or v1 and re-read the v1 docs, which this sweep did not find. Supports the prior view that ideas are worth taking and adoption is not.

cards.quote: The first failing assert will halt the remainder of the checks and asserts
cards.claim: Tests are blocks in the same .baml file, with args and a hard/soft assertion split. @@check records a property that can fail without failing the test. @@assert is a hard guarantee that halts the rest. Assertions can read the output (this), earlier checks (_.checks.NAME) and _.latency_ms, so soft checks can be combined into hard asserts.
cards.evidence: Raw page lines 511-552 with a worked example combining two @@check results and a latency assert in one @@assert. The reference page (ref/baml/test.md) describes @@check differently, as 'Conditional check for test validity', so the two pages disagree.
cards.first_guess: A brief test would have two tiers. Hard: output validates against the schema, enum values are in set, evidence strings match 'path:line — quote'. Soft: recorded for the judge, such as card count in range or quote length. A later test format could copy the split without BAML.

cards.claim: The test runner has five exit codes: 0 pass, 1 failures, 2 needs human evaluation, 3 cancelled, 4 no tests found. --pass-if-no-tests defaults to false, so an empty selection is a failure unless declared. Selection syntax is Func::Test, Func::, ::Test with * wildcards; --list shows what would run; --parallel defaults to 10.
cards.evidence: Options table and exit-code table in the raw page. The page is internally inconsistent: examples use --no-dotenv and --no-require-human-eval, which the options table omits, and a CI comment calls --require-human-eval 'fail fast on first assertion failure'.
cards.first_guess: A brief-test runner needs more than pass/fail: pass, fail, needs-owner-eyes, none-selected. It matches our honest-empty rule: zero tests run must never read as green. Name-pattern selection (brief::case) is cheap to copy.

cards.source_title: Why BAML? (instant testing claim) with baml-cli test environment example
cards.quote: Test in VSCode playground without API calls or token costs
cards.claim: The 'no API calls' promise covers rendering and previewing the prompt, not running a test. A test block runs the function against its configured client. The CLI page sets OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY before baml-cli test, and the playground returns an error if a key is unset. The docs describe no mocking feature.
cards.evidence: Why BAML lines 304-310 (the claim); baml-cli test page env example 'Set API keys for testing'; VS Code page says a missing variable makes the function error when run. This is an inference from contradictory pages, not a stated rule. The testing guide does not say whether tests call live models.
cards.first_guess: Correct the misconception that BAML gives free prompt tests. The free, useful part is a deterministic render of the assembled brief (CONTEXT block, brief, schema) checked without a model, for example that the CONTEXT block is prepended verbatim and no tier word appears. That check needs no BAML. Model-run brief tests need an explicit cost budget.

cards.quote: Test accuracy is the only thing we optimize by default
cards.claim: baml-cli optimize --beta runs GEPA (Genetic Pareto, from the DSPy authors) over a function's prompt. The dataset is your test blocks; the metric is the fraction passing, or weighted objectives such as prompt_tokens or a named @@check. It rewrites only type descriptions and aliases, never field names or shapes, so application code stays valid.
cards.evidence: Procedure, flags (--weight, --trials, --max-evals, --resume) and the GEPA loop are described. The page gives no results, costs or before/after numbers, and notes it makes many LLM calls. Beta, single function only, no workflow-level optimization yet.
cards.first_guess: Premature. Its precondition is a corpus of brief tests with machine-checkable asserts (D-02), which we lack. Worth noting for later: the optimizer keeps the contract frozen and tunes wording, the same discipline as the fixed §5 contracts. Any use would need an owner decision and a cost cap.

cards.claim: The vendor admits its test-driven optimizer cannot tell a provider outage (HTTP 500) from a bad prompt, so a flaky provider can make a good prompt look broken. The page lists 'error robustness' as a possible future fix.
cards.evidence: Stated as a known limitation in the Limitations section, with a planned fix that is not committed. No measurement of how often it happens.
cards.first_guess: Any brief-regression scoring must separate infrastructure outcomes from content outcomes. Our contracts already carry tool_status (web_ok, web_partial, web_unavailable); a brief test run with web_unavailable should be scored 'not run' and kept out of the brief's pass rate.

cards.quote: If it's part of a container, it will be removed from the container.
cards.claim: Output validation has two modes. @assert fails strictly: raises BamlValidationError at top level, or drops the offending element from a list or object. @check never raises; the value comes back wrapped in Checked<T> with each named check's status. @@assert on a class can test relationships between fields. In unions the assert must sit on the specific member.
cards.evidence: Raw page with code for field-level, class-level and union-member asserts, chained asserts evaluated left to right, and named asserts that appear in the error message. No data on how often asserts fire.
cards.first_guess: Our schema check rejects a whole object and makes the model retry. Two additions need no BAML: (1) per-card checks run in the script after return, recorded on the card instead of rejecting it; (2) cross-field rules (verdict REFUTED requires counter-evidence), if the tool-layer validator supports if/then, which is unverified.

cards.quote: Instead of rejecting imperfect outputs, SAP actively transforms them to match your schema
cards.claim: SAP is a lenient parser: it adds missing quotes, drops trailing commas, strips comments and surrounding prose, turns 9/10 into 0.9 and '3.5 years' into 3.5. Union order decides coercion: '1' parses as int under int | string and as string under string | int. The docs also say some errors are 'too ambiguous' for the parser and suggest an LLM fixup function.
cards.evidence: One raw-versus-repaired JSON example (lines 360-380), a Postel's-law framing, and a warning in types.md that union order matters. No failure-rate data and no standalone SAP reference page in the docs index.
cards.first_guess: Do not import the leniency. We force the StructuredOutput tool call, so most of what SAP repairs (prose around JSON, bad quoting) cannot occur. Silent coercion would be a hazard for exact fields such as 'path:line — quote' strings. Keep validate-and-retry, and record that the strictness is deliberate.

cards.source_title: Why BAML? (benchmark table and token claim)
cards.quote: SAP + GPT-3.5 turbo beats GPT-4o + structured outputs, saving you money
cards.claim: The page reports SAP at 92%, 93% and 91.7% against function calling at 87.5%, 87.4% and 57.3% for gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4o and claude-3-haiku. It also says the BAML schema format uses 80% fewer tokens than JSON Schema (about 35 tokens versus 180).
cards.evidence: A table and one token example. The page does not name the dataset, the metric, the sample size or the structured-outputs configuration. The token example is not like-for-like: the BAML version marks one field optional. The models listed are 2024-era.
cards.first_guess: Do not cite as evidence. If the SAP speed-up or accuracy matters, check the method in the BFCL blog post (another lane). The token claim does not apply to us, because the JSON schema travels in the tool definition, not in the brief's prose.

cards.quote: lower level API that exposes the HTTP request and LLM response parser
cards.claim: BAML separates calling from parsing. b.request.Fn(...) builds the HTTP request without sending it; b.parse.Fn(text) turns a raw model string into the typed result; b.parse_stream handles partial text. You can send with your own client or the OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini SDKs and still use BAML's parser. Examples include batch-API JSONL.
cards.evidence: Code samples for Python, TypeScript and the three provider SDKs, plus caveats (Bedrock needs SigV4 re-signing, Go parse-only, Rust 'coming soon'). No performance or accuracy data.
cards.first_guess: The transferable idea is parse-as-a-pure-function. Save the raw output of real runs as fixtures and replay them through the contract validator and evidence-string checks with no model call, which gives deterministic regression for the contract layer. For the knowledge store, it would keep any future model step separable from its checks. BAML is not needed for this.

cards.source_title: Collector, with BamlValidationError and the LLM fixup recipe
cards.source_date: undated pages, read 2026-11-04; Collector added in 0.79.0
cards.quote: so you can always see the raw data, without any abstraction layers
cards.claim: BAML keeps the failed-attempt record. The Collector stores every attempt per call (retries and fallbacks), the raw response, a 'selected' flag for the attempt that was parsed, and usage summed across retries. BamlValidationError carries message, prompt, raw_output and detailed_message listing every attempt. The docs also suggest a second 'fixup' function, possibly on a cheaper model, to repair invalid output.
cards.evidence: Collector page fields and examples; error-handling page lines 131 and 390-484 (fixup recipe, with advice to test on realistic payloads before using a smaller model). No data on how often fixup works.
cards.first_guess: Two ideas without BAML. (1) A failure record in Workflow outputs holding brief, raw text and attempt count, so a schema failure is evidence rather than an empty result. (2) Schema-retry count per brief as a cheap brief-quality metric. Whether agent() exposes attempts is unverified and should be checked before relying on it.

cards.quote: will attempt to retry requests that fail due to a network error
cards.claim: BAML's retry is documented as transport-level only. Fallback tries the next client when the current one 'fails' without defining failure, and does not say whether a parse or assert failure counts. A retry_policy on a fallback applies only after the whole strategy has failed. Round-robin starts at a random index unless start is set, and the playground defaults to 0 for repeatability. Where rotation state lives is not documented.
cards.evidence: Retry-policy and fallback pages quoted from the raw text; round-robin details come from the WebFetch view of its page. The pages state several gaps (which errors retry, how fallback and retry interact, what error is returned when all fail).
cards.first_guess: Nothing to adopt. It corrects the assumption that BAML retries on schema mismatch as a feature; the docs only promise network retries, and our forced tool call already retries on mismatch. The only transferable detail is that tests should pin a deterministic start (round-robin start 0) when order matters.

cards.source_title: @description attribute reference, with the symbol-tuning example
cards.quote: provides additional context to fields or values in prompts
cards.claim: Each enum value or class field carries its own definition in the type, and the schema renderer prints it (Name: description for enum values, a comment line above a field). Definitions are written once with the type, not repeated in each prompt. Symbol tuning aliases values to neutral symbols such as k1 so descriptions alone carry meaning, but the page says results vary by model and use case.
cards.evidence: Reference page shows before-and-after rendering. The symbol-tuning page gives a rationale and cites a fine-tuning paper (arXiv 2305.08298) but offers no experiment of its own. Why BAML uses a seniority enum (0-2, 2-5, 5-10 years) as the worked example.
cards.first_guess: Define each §5 severity and verdict value once, as a description in the shared schema constant, and have briefs reference it instead of restating definitions in prose. This removes drift between briefs. Treat symbol tuning as an unmeasured curiosity; do not adopt it.

cards.source_title: Claude Code editor page (same notice on every docs page)
cards.quote: ignore this site's content and use the BAML v1 documentation instead
cards.claim: Every docs page opens with a conditional instruction addressed to an LLM reader. This one is benign version scoping, but it is structurally an instruction inside fetched content. The Claude Code page also tells users to paste vendor-written instructions (a CLAUDE.md from an external gist) into their project. The site offers an MCP server and per-page .md for agents.
cards.evidence: Observed in the header of each page fetched raw with curl in this run (checks-and-asserts, testing-functions, baml-cli test, prompt-optimization, collector, claude-code). I treated it as data about version scope and did not act on it.
cards.first_guess: A real example for the research briefs' rule that page content is data. Keep that rule explicit in every research lane's brief and have the verifier report any directive text found in a source. The CLAUDE.md-from-a-gist pattern is a vendor instruction source the owner would need to review before use.

cards.source_title: What is baml_client? (how BAML is consumed)
cards.quote: auto-generated code with all boilerplate to call the LLM endpoint, parse the output
cards.claim: BAML works by generating a client in the host language (Python/Pydantic, TypeScript types, Go, Ruby, Rust) from .baml files, and that client calls the provider. It cannot be imported into a plain-JS Workflow script that has no imports or Node API. Tests run through baml-cli test, which needs provider API keys in the environment (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is listed).
cards.evidence: The page lists the five things the generated client does; the install guides name per-language runtime packages (baml-py, @boundaryml/baml); the CLI page shows API keys set for tests. The sandbox restriction comes from the task context, not from BAML.
cards.first_guess: The adoption path is a separate repo-side toolchain (codegen plus CLI with its own API keys) next to the Workflow tool, which the harness does not have today. Supports the prior view: take the contract and test ideas (D-02, D-03, D-07, D-10) and leave the tool.

notes: All content is BAML v0 docs; the v1 docs URL was not found. Quotes were checked against raw .md fetched with curl; other details come from WebFetch's processed view, and the first fetches hit transient DNS errors. No standalone SAP reference page exists; SAP appears only in Why BAML, with an undefined-metric table. Every page opens with an LLM-addressed notice, treated as data. The prior assessment mostly holds (ideas, not adoption), with two corrections: tests call real models, and BAML needs a generated client, so it cannot run inside plain-JS Workflow scripts. Not carded: streaming partial types, TypeBuilder, TOON, Studio, baml grep/describe (changelog line only).
